匠.meaning: An old woodcutter keeps his <part>axe</part> in a velvet-lined <part>drawer</part> and only takes it out for delicate work: a toothpick, a chess set, a violin from a single log. One careful swing, and a perfect wooden bird pops out. He is a true <kanji>artisan</kanji>.
匠.on: Every Sunday the whole town lines up to watch his carving <sound>show</sound>.
匠.kun: For the finale he carves a tiny <sound>ta</sound>rt, a <sound>coo</sound>k to bake it and a <sound>mee</sound>rkat to eat it.

奨.meaning: A retired <part>general</part> coaches the toddlers' swim class, shouting through a <part>large</part> megaphone: 'Kick! Kick! You were born for this!' One by one the toddlers paddle across, waving. Nobody can <kanji>exhort</kanji> like him.
奨.on: Afterwards the toddlers put on a splashing <sound>show</sound> for their parents.
奨.kun: He rewards each one with <sound>su</sound>shi, then sweeps the <sound>soo</sound>t off the barbecue for seconds.

隅.meaning: A shy robot at the school disco spends all night beside the <part>gumball machine</part>, waving a tiny <part>pennant</part> to the music and pretending to read the price sticker. Then a girl comes over for a gumball and stays to dance. The best things happen in the <kanji>corner</kanji>.
隅.on: One gumball melts in his warm hand into a blob of pink <sound>goo</sound>.
隅.kun: She brings him <sound>su</sound>shi and a <sound>mee</sound>rkat sticker for his chest.

渋.meaning: A tea taster sips a brew that has stewed for a week. Her lips pucker, her face freezes, and she holds up a hand: <part>stop</part>! She gulps <part>water drops</part> from the tap and sucks on <part>ice</part>, but her mouth stays dry and puckered. That tea is <kanji>astringent</kanji>.
渋.on: Her assistant hands her a cup of <sound>jew</sound>el-green tea instead, and it's just as bad.
渋.kun: A <sound>shee</sound>p reading a <sound>boo</sound>k at the next table takes a sip and puckers too.

尻.meaning: A marathon runner pins her number on backwards: a little <part>flag</part> with a big <part>nine</part> flaps from the seat of her shorts. Fans cheer as she jogs past, and every photo shows the same thing: number nine, right on her <kanji>buttocks</kanji>.
尻.on: At the finish line she sits down hard on an ice cream <sound>cone</sound>.
尻.kun: Afterwards she cools off on a <sound>shee</sound>t spread over the <sound>ree</sound>ds by the river.

零.meaning: A queen gives the <part>rain</part> strict <part>orders</part> before her garden party: not one drop. The clouds obey so well that the teapot won't pour, the fountain dries up and the swan sits in an empty bowl. The rain gauge reads <kanji>zero</kanji>.
零.on: In the dry fountain a gliding <sound>ray</sound> flaps sadly, waiting for a drop.
零.kun: Then a <sound>ko</sound>ala spills its tea over a <sound>bo</sound>nsai: the first drop all day.

獲.meaning: A <part>falconer</part> whose bird is too lazy to hunt goes out with a <part>fishhook</part> on a rod instead, casting it into the sky. He hooks a passing kite, a lost hat and, at last, a pancake flipped too high at a picnic. Whatever flies by, he can <kanji>seize</kanji>.
獲.on: The lazy falcon just picks at an old chicken <sound>car</sound>cass on his glove.
獲.kun: On his next cast he hooks an <sound>e</sound>gg sandwich from a <sound>roo</sound>k.

疎.meaning: A man takes off his <part>giant boot</part> at a picnic, and the smell clears the meadow. His friends grab their <part>bundle</part> of blankets, move three fields away and quietly stop inviting him. One stinky boot is enough to <kanji>alienate</kanji> everyone.
疎.on: He ends up eating alone on a squashy <sound>so</sound>fa he dragged out himself.
疎.kun: He eats <sound>u</sound>don and <sound>to</sound>ffee by himself, with no idea what his friends are up to: out of touch.

勉.meaning: A <part>rabbit</part> trains for the forest strongman contest: carrots at dawn, turnips at noon, a pumpkin by dusk, sweating and grunting until a tiny <part>muscle</part> pops up on his arm. He wins by gently lifting a hedgehog. That's real <kanji>exertion</kanji>.
勉.on: He does his lifts on a <sound>ben</sound>ch made from a fallen log.
勉.kun: A <sound>tsu</sound>nami of sweat can't stop him: he chews <sound>to</sound>ffee and keeps on lifting.

怠.meaning: A gardener puts a cactus shaped like a <part>heart</part> on a <part>pedestal</part> in the hall, then goes on holiday for a year. Dust piles up, a spider moves in, the cactus sulks and droops. That's what happens when you <kanji>neglect</kanji> things.
怠.on: The spider hangs her web from the gardener's forgotten <sound>tie</sound>.
怠.kun: Back home, he lies on the couch with an <sound>o</sound>tter, a <sound>ko</sound>ala and a <sound>ta</sound>co, still not dusting.

瞬.meaning: Under a <part>blanket</part> on the sofa, a cat pretends to sleep, her <part>mismatched legs</part> poking out. When her owner unwraps a fish, one <part>eye</part> opens, a <part>claw</part> slides out, the fish vanishes and the eye shuts again. All in a <kanji>wink</kanji>.
瞬.on: The fishbones turn up later, tucked under a cu<sound>shion</sound>.
瞬.kun: Her <sound>ma</sound>ma, napping on the rug, blinks as a <sound>ta</sound>co, then a <sound>ta</sound>rt, vanish too.

拍.meaning: A ship's crew paints their <part>anchor</part> bright <part>white</part> for the harbour parade. As it's lowered, gleaming, into the water, every seal on the rocks slaps its flippers together. The anchor almost seems to bow as the seals <kanji>clap</kanji>.
拍.on: The crew throws each seal a <sound>huck</sound>leberry as thanks.

漫.meaning: A lazy artist sways in a <part>hammock</part> over a pool, doodling a duck with huge eyes. A few <part>water drops</part> splash the page, the ink wobbles, and the duck climbs out and argues with him in a speech bubble. He has drawn a living <kanji>cartoon</kanji>.
漫.on: His other drawing, a cheeky <sound>mon</sound>key, swings off the page too.
漫.kun: Soon a <sound>mee</sound>rkat, the <sound>du</sound>ck and a <sound>ree</sound>f fish are running wild across every page.

蛇.meaning: An <part>insect</part> on the barn <part>roof</part> spots a long green rope with a head like a <part>spoon</part>, sliding toward the milk pail. It rings the alarm bell. The rope flicks a forked tongue and hisses. It's a <kanji>snake</kanji>.
蛇.on: The snake curls up inside an empty cookie <sound>ja</sound>r to hide.
蛇.kun: A <sound>he</sound>n and a <sound>bee</sound> chase it out of the barn.

謀.meaning: Three garden gnomes give a cheery <part>speech</part> about tulips at the flower show. Under their beards they whisper about a certain <part>so-and-so</part> next door with a better lawn, and a midnight plan with a bucket of snails. Gnomes love to <kanji>conspire</kanji>.
謀.on: Plan B is to roll a <sound>bou</sound>lder onto his prize pumpkin.
謀.kun: They plot over a <sound>ha</sound>rp-shaped map, keeping very <sound>ca</sound>lm.

億.meaning: A tailor hangs one hat on a <part>coat hook</part> and has an <part>idea</part>: a hook for every head on Earth. She orders the hooks by the crate, then by the ship. Soon her warehouse holds a <kanji>hundred million</kanji> of them.
億.on: An <sound>oc</sound>topus helps her, hanging eight hats at a time.

傍.meaning: At the regatta, everyone rushes to raise a <part>sail</part> except one man, who leans on a <part>coat hook</part> by the boathouse wrapped in a <part>blanket</part>. He doesn't race and he doesn't cheer; he just likes to <part>stand</part> and watch. He's the perfect <kanji>bystander</kanji>.
傍.on: A <sound>bou</sound>lder rolls past him into the lake, and he only raises an eyebrow.
傍.kun: He stays <sound>ca</sound>lm on the side, eating a <sound>ta</sound>co with <sound>wa</sound>sabi and a bowl of <sound>ra</sound>men.

邸.meaning: A rich penguin builds an ice palace with thirty rooms, a <part>sled</part> parked by the front steps and a gold <part>pennant</part> on the tallest tower. Visitors must wipe their flippers. It's a very grand <kanji>residence</kanji>.
邸.on: He seals every crack in the ice walls with sticky <sound>ta</sound>pe.
邸.kun: The front <sound>ya</sound>rd has a knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld on the gate and a gold <sound>key</sound> for every guest.

掘.meaning: A pirate finds an X on the beach but has no shovel, so he hacks at it with his <part>anchor</part> until the hard sand finally starts to <part>yield</part>. Hours later he hits a chest full of... more maps. Pirates just love to <kanji>dig</kanji>.
掘.on: A black <sound>coot</sound> hops into the hole and waddles off with one of the maps.
掘.kun: He takes a break in the hole with a <sound>ho</sound>tdog.

磁.meaning: A tailor drops her <part>sewing kit</part> on a hike, and pins scatter all over the trail. She sighs, picks up a dull grey <part>stone</part>, and every pin leaps onto it with a click. She keeps it in her pocket forever: a natural <kanji>magnet</kanji>.
磁.on: Back home, it tugs the keys right out of her muddy <sound>jee</sound>p.

浅.meaning: A knight takes a dramatic running dive off the castle wall, cape flying, into the moat, and lands standing up, the <part>water drops</part> barely reaching his ankles. He props his spears on a <part>spear rack</part> and pretends he meant it. The moat is very <kanji>shallow</kanji>.
浅.on: A <sound>sen</sound>try on the wall laughs so hard he drops his helmet in.
浅.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>,' sighs a lady in a <sound>sa</sound>ri, and paddles across in two steps.

浜.meaning: A <part>soldier</part> on leave marches along the shore in full uniform, saluting each wave as the <part>water drops</part> soak his boots. The crabs salute back. He stands guard all day over his favourite stretch of <kanji>seacoast</kanji>.
浜.on: At sunset he oils the creaky <sound>hin</sound>ge of the beach hut door.
浜.kun: A <sound>ha</sound>rp seal and her <sound>ma</sound>ma flop onto the sand beside him.

徹.meaning: A ski instructor wants to <part>bring up</part> a tough bunch of pupils. She sends them up the <part>chairlift</part> in a blizzard with a giant <part>fan</part> blowing snow in their faces, until the cold goes through their jackets, socks and bones. Some winds <kanji>penetrate</kanji> everything.
徹.on: One pupil stays warm by hugging a hot-water bottle shaped like a <sound>tet</sound>ra fish.

酢.meaning: A chef labels a sour bottle 'liquid <part>dynamite</part>' and hangs it from the kitchen <part>coat rack</part> so nobody drinks it. A guest takes a swig anyway: his eyes water, his ears pop, his hair stands up. It was only <kanji>vinegar</kanji>.
酢.on: She pickles a fat <sound>suc</sound>culent in it, just to see what happens.
酢.kun: She splashes the rest of the bottle on the rice for <sound>su</sound>shi.

跳.meaning: A frog visits a fortune teller, who reads a <part>portent</part> in a cracked teacup: 'Great things await across the pond.' The frog plants one <part>foot</part> on a lily pad and, with a single boing, sails over. Nothing like a prophecy to make you <kanji>hop</kanji>.
跳.on: On the far bank he finds a frilly <sound>cho</sound>ker waiting on a reed, just as foretold.
跳.kun: Wearing it, he leaps over a <sound>ha</sound>rp and a fishing <sound>ne</sound>t.

堅.meaning: A palace <part>servant</part> runs the royal bakery with a rule for everything: every <part>pretzel</part> twisted exactly three times, not a speck of <part>soil</part> on any boot, no humming. A baker who sneezes is sent home. She is very <kanji>strict</kanji>.
堅.on: Even her dog must be in its <sound>ken</sound>nel by eight.
堅.kun: Her pretzels bake so hard they dent a <sound>ca</sound>rt and crack a <sound>ta</sound>rt tin.

沼.meaning: Every night the frogs in a muddy hollow make a <part>call</part> so loud it rattles the windows in town. The mayor marches out to complain, steps between the reeds and <part>water drops</part>, and sinks to his knees in mud. He has found the <kanji>marsh</kanji>.
沼.on: The frogs put on a <sound>show</sound> for him while he waits to be pulled out.
沼.kun: He shelters in a muddy <sound>noo</sound>k until his <sound>ma</sound>ma comes to fetch him.

召.meaning: A knight lays down his <part>sword</part>, opens his <part>mouth</part> and sings so sweetly that the dragon creeps out of her cave, curls up at his feet and hands him her gold. Not a single fight. Sometimes it's easier to <kanji>seduce</kanji> a dragon than to beat one.
召.on: She follows him all the way home to the village puppet <sound>show</sound>.
召.kun: He keeps her sweet with <sound>me</sound>lon and <sound>su</sound>shi.

穏.meaning: In a field of <part>grain</part>, a bear lies on her back, one <part>claw</part> combing the stalks like a <part>rake</part>, her <part>heart</part> beating slow. Bees bumble past her nose and crows land on her belly. Nothing in the world is as <kanji>calm</kanji>.
穏.on: A farmer tiptoes past and flicks the <sound>on</sound> switch of her music box for a lullaby.
穏.kun: An <sound>o</sound>tter, a <sound>du</sound>ck and a cat from the next <sound>ya</sound>rd curl up beside her, all <sound>ca</sound>lm.

縦.meaning: A window cleaner abseils down a skyscraper on a single <part>thread</part>, and a spider insists on coming to <part>accompany</part> him on her own silk. Neither drifts left or right; they drop straight down forty floors, side by side. Both lines hang perfectly <kanji>vertical</kanji>.
縦.on: At the bottom the spider finds a dropped <sound>jew</sound>el earring and wears it.
縦.kun: Back on the roof, they share a <sound>ta</sound>co on the <sound>te</sound>rrace.
